name: Ezekiel
bio:
Ezekiel son of Buzi was a priest exiled to Babylon with Jehoiachin, living among the captives by the river Chebar. In the fifth year of that exile, he saw an overwhelming vision of God's glory riding on a throne borne by four living creatures, and was commissioned as a prophet to rebellious Israel (Ezekiel 1:1-3:27).

## 📖 Core Story: A Life of Signs

The LORD made Ezekiel's own body and life a series of living signs. He lay on his side for over a year, bearing symbolic days of Israel's and Judah's punishment, ate meager rationed food, and shaved his head and beard, dividing the hair to show how the besieged city's people would die by sword, famine, and scattering (Ezekiel 4:1-5:17). In a vision, he was shown the elders of Israel secretly worshipping idols within the temple itself, and watched the LORD's glory depart from Jerusalem in judgment (Ezekiel 8:1-11:25) — during which Pelatiah son of Benaiah, one of the corrupt leaders, dropped dead as Ezekiel prophesied, and Ezekiel fell on his face crying out that the LORD would utterly destroy Israel's remnant. He packed his bags and dug through a wall as a sign of the exile to come, and ate and drank trembling to show Judah's coming terror (Ezekiel 12:1-20). Most strikingly, when his own wife died, the LORD forbade Ezekiel from mourning her publicly — no weeping, no funeral customs — as a sign that the people would be too devastated by the temple's destruction even to properly grieve (Ezekiel 24:15-27).

## 📖 Core Story: Watchman, Shepherd, and the Valley of Dry Bones

The LORD appointed Ezekiel a watchman responsible for warning Israel of its sin, and taught through him that each person is accountable for their own righteousness rather than inheriting guilt from their ancestors (Ezekiel 3:16-21; 18:1-32; 33:1-20). He condemned Israel's corrupt leaders as false shepherds who fed themselves while scattering the flock, promising God himself would shepherd his people and raise up "my servant David" over them (Ezekiel 34:1-31). In his most famous vision, Ezekiel was shown a valley full of dry bones that came back to life at the LORD's word, flesh and breath returning to them as a sign that Israel, though it felt utterly dead in exile, would be raised and restored to its land (Ezekiel 37:1-14).

## 📖 Core Story: The Vision of the Restored Temple

In an elaborate closing vision, Ezekiel was shown a magnificent future temple in precise detail, with the Zadokite priests restored to their proper service, a river flowing from the temple that brought life wherever it went, and the land divided among the twelve tribes around a city renamed "The LORD Is There" (Ezekiel 40:1-48:35).
